description: Candidate discovery prompts derived from the AV explanation policy mapping. They prioritise situations whose cause or intent may not already be obvious to a passenger. These prompts rank windows for later review; they do not replace the Gemma explanation gate.

interaction_region: a pedestrian cyclist vehicle or obstacle entering the road or driving path
a road user emerging from behind an occlusion near the vehicle path
a pedestrian or cyclist crossing the road in front of the vehicle
pedestrian_intent: an occluded pedestrian preparing to enter the road unexpectedly
a pedestrian close to the driving path with uncertain crossing intent
a distracted pedestrian moving unpredictably near traffic
proximity_risk: a nearby pedestrian cyclist or vehicle closing rapidly
an obstacle very close to the driving path
traffic requiring sudden braking or avoidance
critical_conflict: an imminent conflict between the vehicle and another road user
cross traffic or an unprotected turn requiring yielding
an emergency vehicle or unusual priority conflict
trajectory_uncertainty: multiple road users with conflicting possible trajectories
a vehicle yielding merging or turning with ambiguous intent
complex intersection traffic with uncertain right of way
unusual_context: roadworks or a construction zone changing the normal route
an accident blocked lane or unexpected road obstacle
poor visibility or severe occlusion around a traffic interaction

negative_prompts: ordinary unobstructed lane following with no immediate conflict
normal traffic moving predictably on a clear road
an empty or routine road scene with no explanation worthy event
a clearly visible pedestrian using a marked crosswalk while the vehicle yields normally
an obvious pedestrian crossing with clear right of way and predictable yielding
a routine stop or yield whose visible cause is immediately understandable
